messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to use rJava as follows, and am a bit stuck.
I have some Java code which uses the source .jar from Standford NLP parser.
http://nlp.stanford.edu/software/lex-parser.shtml
I want to be able to call this code from R.
I have added the Stanford .jar separately to my .jclassPath() using
.jaddClassPath() to that .jar, as well as adding my own classes.

However I get this error, pertaining to the Stanford .jar code:

 java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: edu/stanford/nlp/trees/TreebankLanguagePack

When I use verbose I get this output:

pm <- .jnew("Prob_Modeller")
RJavaClassLoader at 11cfb549.findClass
(edu.stanford.nlp.trees.TreebankLanguagePack)
 - URL loader did not find it: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException:
edu.stanford.nlp.trees.TreebankLanguagePack
RJavaClassLoader.findClass("edu.stanford.nlp.trees.TreebankLanguagePack")
 - trying class path
"/home/simon/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/2.15/rJava/java"
   Directory, can get
'/home/simon/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/2.15/rJava/java/edu/stanford/nlp/trees/TreebankLanguagePack.class'?
YES
 - trying class path "/home/simon/workspace/Stanford_Parser1/bin"
   Directory, can get
'/home/simon/workspace/Stanford_Parser1/bin/edu/stanford/nlp/trees/TreebankLanguagePack.class'?
YES
 - trying class path
"/home/simon/College/LiteraryStats/stanford-parser-2012-07-09/stanford-parser-2012-07-09-sources.jar"
   JAR file, can get 'edu/stanford/nlp/trees/TreebankLanguagePack'? YES
    >> ClassNotFoundException
Error in .jnew("Prob_Modeller") :
  java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError:
edu/stanford/nlp/trees/TreebankLanguagePack

I have tried .jfindClass() but I am not able to locate any of the Stanford
.jar code in this way.
The Java code works independently of R.

I assume I have misunderstood something fundamental about including 3rd
party .jars (since it finds my own class no problem), but I cannot seem to
figure it out.
Ideally I would like to use .jinit() rather than .jpackage() for the time
being.

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you,

Simon

messages.body_plain:
Simon,

are you sure you have compatible Java version for your classes? Check the JVM version you are running with

> .jcall("java/lang/System","S","getProperty","java.version")
[1] "1.6.0_37"

and then check your class files

$ file A.class 
A.class: compiled Java class data, version 50.0 (Java 1.6)

If the class files have been compiled with older JVM than what your'e running, it won't recognize the class files and issues "class not found" error.

Cheers,
Simon

R won't be overloaded since each connection has its own R (although they share the initial image for efficiency).

There is an inherent limit on connections and that is imposed by the OS (# of FDs/sockets). There is no explicit limit of parallel processes in Rserve.

That said, you could have a pool of workers managed by your Java code. However, note that re-use of connections has consequences - you may need to clean up after each connection and run the garbage collector, otherwise your memory usage will rise unnecessarily. Tod,

you are using the *binary* which is compiled against system Java (which on your system is 1.6) - so if you remove Java 1.6 you'll break it. If you want to use Java 1.7, you'll have to re-configure R for Java 1.7 and re-compile rJava to use those settings. Note hat Oracle's Java lives in an entirely different place (/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.7.0_09.jdk) than the system Java (/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework), so it is not interchangeable.

In addition, Oracle Java 1.7 it is not a framework, it's a big mess that was not really designed for OS X, so you have to set it by hand to settings like on Linux - it's pretty painful. Also it requires overrides ... so if you really want to go down the rabbit hole, this is what worked for me:

JAVA_LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.7.0_09.jdk/Contents/Home/jre/lib/server JAVA_LIBS='-L/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.7.0_09.jdk/Contents/Home/jre/lib/server -ljvm' JAVA_CPPFLAGS='-I/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.7.0_09.jdk/Contents/Home/include -I/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.7.0_09.jdk/Contents/Home/include/darwin' R64 CMD javareconf 

Then install rJava from sources (R64 -> install.packages("rJava",type='source')). Note that it's 64-bit only, so it will only work with 64-bit R.

Cheers,
Simon

Apart from legal implications, I don't really want to maintain Java installations on all platforms. The whole point was that Apple was taking care of that on Macs - that's why things "just worked" for years, but unfortunately as the importance of Java fades they jumped off the bandwagon ... Implied from this discussion is that it really takes an effort to be up to date on who's doing what and requires continuous changes to the infrastructure. One could argue that we are now entering the Linux realm where it takes some legwork to get things working - Linux users are accustomed to that so they don't mind, but Mac users simply expect things to work, so this model doesn't work. What is really annoying is that Oracle has dropped the ball so there is no canonical way to build JNI applications anymore. We can blame Oracle, Apple or both, but at least I don't have the resources to step in their place. FWIW, personally, I don't really see this as an issue since I don't have anything that requires Java 1.7 so Apple's Java is just fine - this is the first time I heard anyone installing the Oracle mess (and first time learning that it's so bad). We are still back at Java 1.5 with R supporting OS X 10.5+ so any 1.7 requirements seem outlandish. We are yet to drop 32-bit in R to move to Java 1.6 so that's not a snow I feel I have to shovel yet ;) - I have enough worries with Apple abandoning gcc to worry about Java. But if someone whats to maintain the canonical Java binaries, I'd support that thought - but note that there are fours system versions to worry about so far, so it's not trivial. That said, technically, it would be possible to create a framework that works from Oracle's messy binaries, but one would have to re-do the job with every update which is not something I'd like to subscribe to.

Cheers,
Simon
